UI/UX Designer (f/m/d)

Who We Are: At Hunt St , we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: A specialist agency focused on improving website performance for e-commerce brands by enhancing user experience and increasing conversion rates. They partner with teams to deliver site audits, data-driven redesigns, and strategic growth support aimed at turning existing traffic into revenue.

Role Overview: We are looking for a highly experienced Senior E-commerce UX/UI Designer to help create and optimise high-performing digital experiences for direct-to-consumer brands.

This role is suited to someone who has worked with established global agencies or leading e-commerce brands and can confidently take a project from early strategy through to a complete, development-ready design.

You will work across full website redesigns, new site builds, landing pages, conversion optimisation projects and ongoing website improvements.

Some projects will begin with an established brand and clear guidelines, while others may involve taking limited brand information and turning it into a practical digital design system that can scale across an entire website.

The ideal candidate combines strong visual design skills with commercial thinking, UX strategy and a deep understanding of how customers shop online. Key Responsibilities: Full Website Design
Design complete e-commerce experiences from the ground up, including homepages, collection pages, product pages, cart experiences, navigation, search and supporting content pages.
Translate brand positioning, customer insights and business goals into clear, engaging digital experiences.
Create scalable design systems that can be used consistently across templates, sections and future pages.
Design with development feasibility, responsiveness and Shopify implementation in mind.
Produce detailed, development-ready designs that minimise ambiguity during the build process.
UX and Conversion Strategy
Understand the full customer journey, from discovery and consideration through to purchase and retention.
Identify the questions, concerns and barriers customers may experience throughout the buying journey.
Structure pages and content to improve clarity, trust, product understanding and conversion.
Balance brand storytelling with usability and commercial performance.
Design for a wide variety of products, customer types and purchase journeys.

At Flying Bisons , we're rebuilding our design process around a simple principle: interactive prototypes before static screens. Every project, every module. We need people who can take a brief and produce 70-80% of the design as a working prototype — fast — so our senior strategists can focus on what to build, and our craft designers can focus on making it beautiful.
We call this the AI-First Designer role. You are the engine of production in our Pyramid framework: you sit between the people who define the product and the people who polish it to perfection. You generate the bulk of the work. Speed and iteration are your core skills.
What you'll actually do
You'll join project teams alongside Strategic & Senior UX Designers (who own strategy and scope) and Top UI Designers (who own visual direction and craft). Your job starts when the concept is approved and the scope is locked.
In practice, your week looks like this: you get a module brief — "build the checkout flow for a B2B e-commerce platform, here are the user stories, here's the approved visual direction." You open your AI tool of choice, start prompting (probably talking, not typing), and within a couple of hours you have an interactive prototype with real interactions, real copy, and real edge cases.

You share it with the team async. They give feedback. You iterate. When it's solid, you hand it to a UI designer who takes it to 100% in Figma — design system compliance, pixel perfection, all states, documentation.
You'll also be involved in concept workshops, where you build rough interactive prototypes live during the session so the team can react to something real, not abstract sketches.
And honestly — you'll be a bit of an evangelist. You'll be one of the first people in this role at Flying Bisons . Your work will set the standard for how the rest of the team thinks about AI-first design.

You think in a different paradigm. When you hear "design a settings page," your instinct isn't to open Figma and start placing rectangles. Your instinct is to describe what the settings page should do, prompt an AI tool, get a working version, and start shaping it from there. Generation first, refinement second.
You're fast. You can go from a text or voice brief to a clickable, multi-screen prototype in under 2 hours. You don't aim for perfection on the first pass — you aim for something real enough that people can click through it and give meaningful feedback.
You're fluent in AI design tools. You work regularly with at least 2-3 of these: Magic Patterns, v0, Bolt, Lovable, Cursor, Claude Code, Figma Make. You know their strengths and weaknesses. You know when to switch tools.

You have design sensibility. You're not a pixel-perfect UI specialist — that's a different role on the team. But you know when something looks wrong, when spacing is off, when a flow doesn't make sense. You care about the end experience, even at the 70% stage.
You can hold product thinking. You understand user stories, flows, edge cases, empty states, error handling. When you generate a prototype, you think about what happens when the list is empty, when the user makes a mistake, when there are 3 items vs. 300. You don't just build the happy path.
